title: What Holds It Together
subtitle: Industrial ingredients that change how food feels.
description: Thickeners, stabilisers and emulsifiers are added to modify the consistency and structure of food. They serve an industrial function, not a nutritional one.
why_body: Minimally processed foods do not contain texture modifiers. Their presence signals that a product has been significantly reformulated from its basic ingredients. According to the NOVA classification system (FAO, 2019), texture modifiers are one of the defining markers of ultra-processed food.
what_body: BOTIA detects ingredients classified as thickeners, stabilisers or emulsifiers: xanthan gum (E415), carrageenan (E407), guar gum (E412), locust bean gum (E410), gellan gum (E418), mono- and diglycerides (E471), lecithins (E322), and others. Some — like carrageenan — are under active scientific review for their effects on gut health.
can_1: Detect texture modifiers declared on the label.
can_2: Flag ingredients under active scientific review for gut health effects.
can_3: Signal ultra-processed food markers based on NOVA classification.
cannot_1: Tell you whether this product is harmful to your gut personally.
cannot_2: Quantify your exposure to texture modifiers across your diet.
closing: For more detail on specific texture modifiers, explore the ingredient pages linked above.
